criteria.rationale: Examined signatures and callers: ReadOnlyIndex keeps its signature, ReadOnlyIndexContext and GitReadError are additions, reportChangedFiles is internal, report keeps exit 0 and no MCP schema or record format changes. Error wording changes are covered by the findings.

D2 removes the stat-then-open race behind N22 and keeps FIFOs from blocking; D1 and L1 rest on measured Git behaviour; D3 binds the lookup to the caller's context, which addresses R2's deadline. D3's locale claim holds for the diff read only, recorded as N12. The sealed design assessment lists no structural deltas.

The spec's artifacts list was extended with the new linux test and the ledger file, matching the 13 implementation files; artifact-check strict exits 0; remaining items are recorded as spec follow-ups.

Examined the open and hand-over paths: non-blocking open judged by fstat, 512 MiB bound, sanitised Git environment, 0600 private copy removed after use. Git stderr now reaches findings and the local report; it holds paths and no secrets in the probes, noted as low in N15.

The round adds one error helper, one context variant and two replaceable call variables for the fallback test, all small and used. The text heuristic is the cheapest classification and stops being adequate where Git's message is translated or names a revision (N12, N13).

findings.action: A plain pose report silently drops a failed index read in a pt-BR locale. report.go:322 runs git status without LC_ALL=C, GitReadError marks an index failure only when stderr contains the English word 'index', and report.go:201-204 discards every unmarked error. With LANG=pt_BR.UTF-8 and a corrupt index (bad signature, bad version or unknown extension: git says 'arquivo de índice corrompido') the report exits 0, prints no warning and writes '_No files detected_'. Round 1's commit warned here. The same rule silences non-index failures outside the stated non-repository case (a broken .git/config or HEAD gave the same false report). Contradicts D3 ('in any locale') and the spec's API contract. Reproduced with overlay probes.
Match Git's index diagnostics rather than the bare word, excluding revision errors, and drop the doubled prefix.
findings.rationale: The substring test 'index' marks revision failures as index failures: an unknown --changed-from named feature/index-rework yields 'the index cannot be read: exit status 128: fatal: bad revision' and drops the revision-unknown wording; report --since does the same. The scope message also repeats itself ('git diff X failed: git diff failed:').

findings.action: Capture the lookup's stderr and classify it like the other reads.
findings.rationale: The index lookup still discards Git's standard error and marks every failure ErrIndexUnreadable: outside a repository, or with a broken config or HEAD, scope selection says 'cannot be located: the index cannot be read: exit status 128', naming the wrong failure without its cause.

findings.action: Write a bounded one-line marker in the report and bound the stderr kept in the error.
findings.rationale: The error text, including Git's whole multi-line stderr and in some cases the checkout's absolute path, is written into the versioned report: continuation lines fall outside the Files Changed list item. GitReadError (git_worktree_reads.go:102-110) puts no bound on the stderr it keeps.

findings.rationale: Several round 2 behaviours have no failing test: replacing ReadOnlyIndexContext(ctx) with ReadOnlyIndex (D3), removing LC_ALL=C, removing the ErrIndexUnreadable wrap on a hand-over failure, restoring the error on a memfd write failure, removing the non-repository silencing and removing the report marker each leave the focused tests green.
